name: Gjirokastër
title: Holidays in Gjirokastër
intro: Albania's 'city of stone', a hillside of Ottoman tower houses with slate roofs below a huge castle, in a valley of mountains. Here's what Gjirokastër is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The Old Bazaar street of Gjirokastër, lined with carpets and craft shops
facts_note: Euros are often accepted in tourist areas, but prices are better in lek. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April, May, September and October are best for walking the steep streets. July and August are very hot but combine well with the beaches at Saranda and Ksamil, an hour away. Winter is cold and rainy.

things.name: Gjirokastër Castle
things.blurb: A huge hilltop fortress with old cannons and a war plane.

things.name: Skenduli House
things.blurb: A traditional Ottoman tower house, shown by its family.

things.name: Old Bazaar
things.blurb: Stone lanes of craft shops and cafés.

things.name: Cold War tunnel
things.blurb: A bunker built under the city in communist times.

things.name: Blue Eye spring
things.blurb: A deep, glowing blue spring in the woods, 40 minutes away.

things.name: Butrint
things.blurb: Ancient ruins by a lagoon near Saranda, about 1 hour 15 minutes away.

faqs.question: Is Gjirokastër worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's a UNESCO-listed old town, unlike anywhere else, and easy to add to a beach holiday in southern Albania.

faqs.question: How do you get to Gjirokastër?
faqs.answer: Fly into Tirana, about 3 hours away, or to Corfu and take the ferry to Saranda, an hour away.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Gjirokastër?
faqs.answer: One or two days covers the town and the Blue Eye.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Gjirokastër?
Is Albania safe to visit?
faqs.answer: Albania is generally considered safe and welcoming to visitors. Check the latest GOV.UK travel advice before you book.
